chunks: We used to pray to Him erstwhile; He is the just and merciful.

key_terms.الْبَرُّ: The Benevolent / The Source of Goodness
key_terms.نَدْعُوهُ: We pray to Him / We supplicate to Him

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God's mercy and benevolence in response to supplication?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to demonstrate the reciprocal nature of divine mercy, where human supplication (dua) is met with God's inherent goodness (al-Barr) and compassion (al-Rahim). It underscores the theological principle that God’s attributes are not merely reactive but foundational, encouraging believers to approach prayer with confidence in His benevolent response. This perspective aligns with the Shia emphasis on the accessibility of God to His servants through sincere invocation.
